Research

Reflex gives a G1 onboard vision for catching thrown boxes

The research combines visual prediction with whole-body reactions.

Reflex research team ↗9 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 18

Three training stages

Reflex first learns catching control, then estimates box dynamics from delayed or partial observations. An RGB-D encoder subsequently learns visual grounding while the whole-body controller stays fixed.

Physical and simulated results

Reported physical success is 65% at 2.5 metres and 40% at 5 metres. The 85.7% RGB-D success figure belongs to simulation, not physical trials.

Reading the demonstrations

Videos cover distance, box size, payload and handover. The interactive scene replays recorded successful catches, so it cannot replace aggregate experimental success rates.
